126458.overview: Parashooter is a shoot 'em up game, developed and published by Emerson Radio Corp., which was released in 1982.

126459.overview:
This is a sequel to Phoenix.

On the first screen, you must shoot swooping aliens while not getting shot by them. At some point, an alien will create a shield across the screen just above your ship that will require you to shoot holes through to destroy more aliens. Be aware, however, that the alien shots are not slowed at all and can still kill you.

On the second screen, you must shoot or avoid a phoenix(es) shots but the object is to shoot the alien in the mothership above. You can also shoot the phoenix(es) themselves for points.

On the third screen, you must maneuver between parked ships, without hitting any, to dock at your spot at the top. Once you do this, the game goes to the first screen only harder.

There are game selections to choose to also play only the first, second or third screens, with each wave getting harder.

464672.overview:
Video-Panzerspiel is a tank-themed action-strategy game released for the Palladium Video Computer Game, a German clone of the Emerson Arcadia 2001 system. The game was part of Palladium’s catalog of cartridges adapting popular arcade-style and tactical concepts for the home market in Germany.

Players control a tank on a simple battlefield, navigating to avoid obstacles and engaging enemy tanks. The objective is to destroy opposing units while preserving one’s own tank, emphasizing strategic positioning and timing. Like other Palladium titles, the gameplay is straightforward, focusing on reflexes and basic tactical decisions rather than complex simulation.

Graphically, Video-Panzerspiel employs blocky sprites to represent tanks and projectiles. The battlefield is rendered as a static grid or simple background, while collisions and firing are indicated with basic audio cues, such as beeps or short tones. The controls are minimal, allowing easy access for casual players.
